standard_prerequisites.name: The sheaf condition

standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the sheaf condition verified for the presheaf limit.

core_obligations: The sheaf property (proof lines 1907-1921): given a compatible family over a covering for the presheaf limit, the projections produce compatible families for each sheaf in the diagram, which have unique amalgamations; the author then uses the sheaf property of one member of the diagram to show that the transition maps carry the amalgamations to one another, giving an element of the limit over the object.
The closing verification (proof lines 1922-1923): the author leaves to the reader the check that the element so obtained restricts to the given compatible family.
proof_roadmap: Show that the presheaf limit satisfies the sheaf condition.
Use the sheaf property in each degree and the transition maps to build a compatible system.
Leave the final restriction check to the reader, then conclude the limit statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the limit of a diagram of sheaves exists and coincides with the limit computed in presheaves (statement lines 1896-1904). The proof is a complete argument: the presheaf limit is shown to satisfy the sheaf condition by projecting a compatible family to each member of the diagram, using the sheaf property there to build a compatible system through the transition maps (proof lines 1907-1921); and the author leaves to the reader only the check that the resulting element restricts to the given family (proof lines 1922-1923). The non-formal content is the construction of the compatible system. The claim is H2: a written-out verification with the closing check noted.
